title: Base64 Overview
content: Base64 is an encoding scheme that represents binary data using uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, plus signs, slashes, and optional equals padding.

title: Base64 Character Pattern
content: Base64 strings usually contain A-Z, a-z, 0-9, plus, slash, and equals signs. Their length is commonly divisible by 4.

title: Base64 Padding
content: Base64 encoded strings may end with one or two equals signs as padding. Padding helps complete the encoded block size.

title: Base64 SVM Features
content: The SVM can identify Base64 using engineered features such as base64 character ratio, lowercase ratio, plus slash count, equals count, entropy, and length divisibility.

title: Base32 Overview
content: Base32 is an encoding scheme that uses uppercase letters A-Z and digits 2-7. It often includes equals signs as padding.

title: Base32 Character Pattern
content: Base32 strings are usually uppercase-heavy and do not contain lowercase letters, plus signs, or slashes.

title: Base32 Padding
content: Base32 commonly uses equals signs as padding. The encoded string may end with multiple equals signs.

title: Base32 SVM Features
content: The SVM can identify Base32 using engineered features such as base32 character ratio, uppercase ratio, digit ratio, equals count, entropy, and absence of plus or slash symbols.

title: Morse Overview
content: Morse code represents letters and numbers using dots and dashes. Words are often separated by slash characters.

title: Morse Character Pattern
content: Morse text mainly contains dots, dashes, spaces, and slashes. This makes it visually different from Base64 and Base32.

title: Morse Decoding
content: Morse code can be decoded by mapping each dot-dash sequence to its corresponding letter or number.

title: Morse SVM Features
content: The SVM can identify Morse using engineered features such as morse ratio, dot dash ratio, symbol ratio, and space ratio.

title: LLM Role
content: The LLM role in CRYPTO AI is limited to extracting the cypher_text from messy natural language input. It does not classify or decode the cipher.

title: SVM Role
content: The SVM-RBF classifier predicts the cipher type based on engineered numerical features extracted from cypher_text.

title: Decoder Role
content: The decoder tools decode the cypher_text only after the SVM predicts the cipher type. This keeps decoding deterministic and avoids LLM hallucination.

title: DBSCAN Role
content: DBSCAN detects density-based clusters and identifies anomalous cipher patterns as noise points.

title: FCM Role
content: Fuzzy C-Means assigns soft cluster memberships, helping the system understand overlapping patterns between cipher samples.

title: SHAP Role
content: SHAP explains which engineered features influenced the SVM prediction, such as base32 ratio, entropy, or dot dash ratio.

title: SARIMA Role
content: SARIMA forecasts trends in cipher-related numerical features over time, helping estimate future risk or complexity changes.

title: Drift Detection Role
content: Drift detection checks whether forecasted behavior indicates a major change in the data distribution.

title: Dynamic Reclustering Role
content: Dynamic reclustering can rebuild clustering and classification outputs when massive drift is detected.

title: API Action Role
content: The API Action layer executes or logs an alert when the system decides that an action is required or when demo mode forces an action.

title: LangSmith Role
content: LangSmith provides observability by tracing the full CRYPTO AI pipeline from extraction to SVM prediction, decoding, RAG retrieval, reporting, and API action.

title: RAG KNN Role
content: RAG-KNN retrieves the most relevant knowledge snippets from the local cipher knowledge base to support the final explanation and LLM report.

title: TF-IDF Role
content: TF-IDF converts text documents into numerical vectors so that KNN can compare the user case with knowledge base documents.

title: KNN Role
content: KNN retrieves the nearest knowledge documents to the current cipher case using cosine similarity over TF-IDF vectors.
